newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The Zairean peace talks between President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila could take place on a South African Navy supply ship in international waters off the coast of Zaire and the Angolan enclave of Cabinda.
- A white paper on water due to be launched at a major public function this week by Water and Forestry Minister Kader Ismal has been rejected by the cabinet committee on economic and social affairs.

- Government is planning a substantial expansion of the Post Office's services to boost revenue, including a possible takeover of SA's social pension payouts, a role in tax collection and a bid to run the planned national lottery.

- The development corporations of South Africa's North West and Free State provinces have reached a stalemate in their dispute over 50 million rand worth of assets that previously belonged to a Bophuthatswana homeland parastatal.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The SABC, the national broadcaster, has asked the government to help to cover the estimated 100 million rand cost of retrenching 1,400 members of staff, Zwelakhe Sisulu, the SABC's chief executive, said at the weekend.

- Local economists were surprised and confused last Friday by a suggestion from Chris Stals, the Reserve Bank governor, that "monetary policy may ot be restrictive eough" and that another interest increase may be necessary to slow credit extension.

- The signing of a sizable aluminium deal between Tongaat Hulett and Norsk Hydro, a large Norwegian holding company, could stimulate could stimulate more Norwegian investment in South Africa, Alec Erwin, the trade and industry minister, said last week.

- Unbundling and black economic empowerment deals helped boost the value of mergers and acquisition transactions last year to 62,2 billion rand, 43 percent higher than the 1995 figure, Ernst & Young said in its yearly merger and acquisitions survey published last week.
THE STAR
- Thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees returned to a camp south of Kisangani on Monday, telling of a horrific slaughter that prompted their exodus last week.
- The Truth Commission has confirmed that Freedom Front leader Constand Viljoen can hand in a "general" amnesty application for political crimes in the run-up to the 1994 election.
- The body of a woman was found hanging from a tree at Vlakfontein farm in Benoni on Monday while a baby boy was still tied to her back, East Rand police said.
SAKE-BEELD

- The ever-growing debt of electricity users is posing a major threat to state-utility Eskom. Users already owe Eskom 1.4 billion rand, which is equal to half of the firm's yearly net income from the sale of electricity.
- Alexkor, the government diamond company based in Namaqualand, is at a crossroads and will have to take drastic steps to restructure.
- More than 50 million cartons of citrus are ready to be exported to 60 countries.
